---
title: "Exploratory Data Analysis"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

df <- palmerpenguins::penguins

summary(df)
```

The dataset contains 344 penguins from three species observed between 2007 and 2009. Most measurement variables have two missing values, while sex has 11; this missingness should be considered before modeling or comparing groups.

```{r}
df |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_values"
  )
```

```{r}
#| include: false

plot_df <- df |>
  filter(!is.na(bill_length_mm), !is.na(body_mass_g))

excluded_n <- nrow(df) - nrow(plot_df)
```

The plot excludes `r excluded_n` penguins with missing values for bill length, or body mass.

```{r}
plot_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = "y ~ x") +
  labs(
    title = "Penguin Bill Length vs Body Mass",
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Body Mass (g)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Across all penguins, longer bills are generally associated with greater body mass, but the species form distinct clusters. All three species show positive fitted slopes, with Gentoo’s steepest; the overall pattern partly reflects both within-species association and differences among species.
